subtopics.title: Simplify expressions with rational exponents
subtopics.exposition: The exponent laws can also be applied to expressions with rational exponents. To simplify a product of powers of the same base with rational exponents, add the exponents: in 2x^(1/2) × 4x^(-1/2) the powers of x combine as x^(1/2 - 1/2). When simplifying 2x^(1/2) × 4x^(-1/2), the coefficients 2 and 4 are multiplied to give 8. Adding the exponents 1/2 and -1/2 gives the exponent 0, so 2x^(1/2) × 4x^(-1/2) becomes 8x^0. A power with exponent 0 is replaced by 1, so 8x^0 = 8(1) = 8. A rational exponent on a fraction is applied to the numerator and to the denominator separately: (1/5^3)^(1/3) = 1^(1/3) / 5^(3 · 1/3). A power raised to a rational exponent has its exponents multiplied: (5^3)^(1/3) = 5^(3 · 1/3).

subtopics.title: Evaluate numeric rational powers
subtopics.exposition: To simplify a decimal base raised to a rational exponent, write the base as a fraction and simplify it. The decimal 0.008 is written as the fraction 8/1000, so (0.008)^(1/3) = (8/1000)^(1/3). The fraction 8/1000 is simplified to 1/125, so (8/1000)^(1/3) = (1/125)^(1/3). Evaluating by this method gives (0.008)^(1/3) = 1/5. The denominator 125 is rewritten as the prime power 5^3, so (1/125)^(1/3) = (1/5^3)^(1/3). The book writes a decimal number with a comma as the decimal separator, for example 0.008.
